Hi Hannah,

I'm reaching out from Riverbend University's Center for Applied Linguistics. We run a semester-long undergraduate research program where students build prototypes that rely on LLM access. Our IT budget is limited; we are hoping Redwood can provide an academic/sample grant — roughly $3k in credits — to support 30 students over the fall term.

Attached is a brief grant request and a letter from our department head. Could you advise on eligibility and what information you need to approve a promotional credit allocation to our account?

Thanks,
Emily

Riverbend University

Hi Emily — thanks for the note and the clear request. We're excited about programs like yours. A few quick questions so I can route this correctly to our academic promotions and finance teams:

- Is the project strictly non-commercial (student prototypes only)?
- Do you need credits on a single central account or distributed to individual student emails?
- Do you have any procurement/PO requirements for grant acceptance?

If the answers are non-commercial and a single account is fine, we typically approve an initial education promo (credits voucher) that the instructor redeems in the Console; further top-ups can go through a quick review. I'll loop in Marissa (programs) and Aditya (sales finance) to confirm amounts and any terms.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Sales Manager | Education Programs
Redwood Inference

Note: Please attach a signed assurance or memorandum of understanding if possible.
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 09:18:00 -04:00
Subject: Fwd: Requesting credits for student research initiative

Looping in Evelyn from programs. Per our academic policy, we can grant up to $5k in promotional credits for accredited universities with a brief MOU. Standard program terms apply (non-commercial research only, 12-month expiry, no resale). For distribution, we prefer a single account with an instructor-managed API key to keep audit logs consolidated.

Action items for approval:
- Confirm institution accreditation (Emily attached letter covers this).
- Finance to confirm no PO required for promo grants under $5k; otherwise we need a PO and invoice.

Aditya — can you confirm whether we need a billing exception for the $3k allocation and whether a promo code or direct Console credit is preferred operationally?

Thanks — Marissa
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Marissa/Hannah — finance confirms no PO required for promotional grants ≤ $5k. We can issue either:

1) A promo voucher code (redeemable in Console) — faster, self-serve for the instructor; OR
2) Direct allocation applied to the Riverbend organization account (requires us to create the org record and attach terms).

Operational preference: voucher code for speed. For auditing, ask the instructor to provide the account/org ID when they redeem so we can tag the allocation. I can approve $3k today if programs signs off.

I'll prepare an internal approval note for records and the promo code once we have programs sign-off and the signed assurance letter.

- Aditya
